llm.reply:
The knowledge graph links Lynch syndrome to a set of genes, led by the DNA mismatch repair family, and the gene with identifier NCBIGene:4292 is mutL homolog 1 [10]. The condition itself has a disease record named Lynch syndrome [7]. Several clinical studies on hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer and Lynch syndrome were also retrieved [1].

## Mismatch Repair Genes

NCBIGene:4436 is mutS homolog 2 [11]. NCBIGene:2956 is mutS homolog 6 [8]. NCBIGene:5395 is PMS1 homolog 2, mismatch repair system component [14]. NCBIGene:5378 is PMS1 homolog 1, mismatch repair system component [13]. NCBIGene:27030 is mutL homolog 3 [6].

## Other Linked Genes

NCBIGene:4072 is epithelial cell adhesion molecule [9]. NCBIGene:7048 is transforming growth factor beta receptor 2 [16]. NCBIGene:999 is cadherin 1 [17]. NCBIGene:4763 is neurofibromin 1 [12]. NCBIGene:6224 is ribosomal protein S20 [15].

## Clinical Studies

One study is Implementation of a New Strategy to Identify HNPCC Patients [1]. Another is Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer in Taiwan-Related Genetic Study and Clinical Applications [2]. A third is Psychosocial Aspects of Genetic Testing for Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colon Cancer [3]. There is also the Registry for Women Who Are At Risk Or May Have Lynch Syndrome [5].

## Records and Literature

MedGen holds a concept titled Lynch syndrome [19]. PubTator indexes the related entity Colorectal Neoplasms Hereditary Nonpolyposis [23]. The literature includes a review titled Lynch Syndrome Genetics and Clinical Implications. [30]. It also includes a paper titled Differentiating Lynch-like from Lynch syndrome. [22].
